8.14.2.en: The hypocrite is like the tree that everyone desires to enjoy the sight of, but when hypocrisy, like the axe, strikes its roots, it loses its vitality and its fruit and its beauty. He becomes like the foolish virgins who have all the appearance of the wise virgins, but have no oil, so they do not carry light that comes out of their lamps. They remain in the darkness, unable to enter the bridal chamber of the heavenly Bridegroom, where darkness can have no place.

8.14.3.en: * [If God must destroy him, his place will deny him.] The hypocrite is destroyed from his place when he is removed from the praise of the present life by the intervention of death. But the inner witness denies him, and thus destroys him, and proves that God does not know him, since in justice He condemns the life of the pretender. The Truth does not know him, nor does He recognize the good works he practiced. For he did not practice them with a sound purpose in thought. Therefore when God comes to judgment He will say to the foolish virgins: [Verily I say unto you, I know you not] (Mt 25:12). For seeing the corruption of the thought, He condemns even the incorruption that is in the body.

8.14.5.en: * [If one is swallowed up, the place will deny him.] By swallowing up in Holy Scripture is meant what the prophet Isaiah said: [Death shall be swallowed up for ever, and the Lord God shall wipe away every tear from every face] (Isa 25:8). For this reason "his place shall deny him", because the swallowing by which death swallowed Adam (cf. Rom 5:17), which urged him to disobey the commands of God (Gen 2:17), swallows death itself to its destruction.

8.14.6.en: But "his place shall deny him". What place? Perhaps this concerns death, for the place of the traitor is death.

8.14.7.en: It can also be said: [He wipes away every tear from every face] (Isa 25:8). (The Lord Christ) made Adam glorious by His crucifixion, death and resurrection, and turned the craftiness of the accuser back upon the enemy. He saved Adam, and the curse was wrested away by the One to whom all that exists belongs.

8.15.0.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem This is the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall another grow [19].

8.15.1.en: This is the fate of the wicked hypocrite, for he thought that his hope would turn into joy. Yet he is uprooted like the tree and another takes his place, in the same place.

8.16.0.en: 20 "Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers. 21 When he shall fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing, 22 They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought."

8.16.1.en: After reviewing painful images of the hypocritical man, meaning by him "Job", he presents to us a joyful image of the perfect man, asking Job to leave his hypocrisy and walk the way of perfection. Perhaps while describing what the perfect man enjoys of God's good pleasure in him and in his sacrifices and offerings, and how his mouth is filled with joy and his lips with shouting, and how he enjoys victory over the enemies whom the Lord grieves, he set this before himself and his two friends Eliphaz and Zophar. It is as though he is calling Job to leave his hidden evil and follow the example of his three companions, who in Bildad's mind are perfect. Bildad sees that the tent of the wicked Job no longer exists, whereas they have their dwellings fortified by God. Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem sees that what Bildad said concerning those perfect in the Lord applies to Job, for while he accuses him of evil and calls him to perfection, behold, he defends him without knowing it.

8.16.2.en: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers [20].

8.16.3.en: In the conclusion of his speech Bildad summarizes his moral theological understanding, which is that God does not reject the perfect man, but answers his request even if it seems that He has rejected him. And He turns his mourning into dancing and joy, and fills his inner mouth with spiritual laughter. Then those who reproached him will be put to shame when they see that he has returned to his former prosperity and joy. Their clothing will be shame and disgrace when they see him crowned with glory. Corresponding to this, God does not support evildoers and destroys their tents. Perhaps he wanted here to hint at Job as being wicked, whose cries God did not hear, and whose dwelling He utterly destroyed together with his family.

8.16.4.en: This is Bildad's judgment on Job, whom he advises to turn back from his evil and repent, and whom he accuses of evil and hypocrisy. He judged him not knowing what is in his heart or in his mind, indeed not knowing what passed between God and Satan in heaven.

8.16.5.en: * In any case Job is not a wicked man, nor a wicked soldier. On the contrary, one can apply to him what Bildad added, unaware that while he accuses him, behold, he becomes his defender.

8.16.6.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * Certainly when the perfect one appears in the judgment, He at once lifts up the simple and despised from their condition and glorifies them, and shatters the greatness of those of evil mind and condemns them... So God does not stretch out His hand to the evil in mind, since all who seek earthly glory He leaves below, even if they have done good things, whatever their goodness, for He does not grant them the heavenly joys.

8.17.0.en: When he shall fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing [21].

8.17.1.en: Bildad calls Job to leave evil and walk in the way of perfection, so that he may enjoy spiritual laughter and joy in the Lord. This is the joy which the true believer enjoys, bearing within him our Lord Jesus, who gladdens hearts.

8.17.2.en: Christianity is a call to enjoy the joy of heaven; for if our Christ came down from heaven incarnate, it was only to carry us to His heavens as a bride rejoicing in her Bridegroom; for this reason the Apostle Paul calls us while in prison: [Rejoice at all times, and I say, my brethren, rejoice](b).

8.17.3.en: St. Anba Antony sees that joy is the food of the soul; without it the soul hungers and dies. The inner heavenly joy supports the soul in its exile from its heavenly homeland, and prepares the body to bear a mark akin to the spiritual, so that it is prepared to become a spiritual body on the great Day of the Lord.

8.17.4.en: * As trees cannot grow if they do not drink water, so the soul, if it does not receive heavenly joy, cannot grow and ascend to the heights. But the souls that have received the Spirit and heavenly joy are those that can rise to the heights.. For the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven were revealed to them while still in this body, and they found boldness before God in everything, and all their requests were fulfilled.

8.17.5.en: * The soul is always nurtured by this joy and made happy by it, and by it ascends to heaven, for like the body it has its spiritual food.

8.17.6.en: St. Antony the Great * He who looks in himself to our Lord, and whose soul is mingled with His light, is filled in his heart with joy.

8.17.7.en: The Spiritual Elder * It is not fitting for a man to laugh at all times and be like a laughing animal... [A fool lifteth up his voice with laughter] (Sir 21:23). But the wise man smiles in a way that does not attract notice...

8.17.8.en: On the other hand, it is fitting for a man not to be gloomy and sullen, but only serious. For it is better for one who has stern features to smile.

8.17.9.en: The smile is one of the principles of education and its subjects.

8.17.10.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * True joy is the joy of the other life, where the soul is not tormented and torn by desire.

8.17.11.en: St. John Chrysostom * "The kingdom of God is within you"(c) means the joy that the Holy Spirit plants in your hearts, being an icon and pledge of the eternal joy that the souls of the saints enjoy.

8.17.12.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * [The mouths of the saved are filled with laughter, and their lips with gladness]. Take heed, O Bildad, and look quickly at the weight of your words... But it will not "be filled" in truth until afterward in the age to come, where grace awaits Job, in that he is a saved man. There too he will enjoy lips filled with the work of grace, that is, filled with thanksgiving to God.

8.17.13.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * Christ proclaimed the laughter that comes from joy and gladness, as Holy Scripture says in Job: [Truth fills the mouth with laughter] (Job 8:21). Perhaps for this reason one of the Fathers (the Patriarch Isaac) was named "Laughter", because the name means divine gladness.

8.17.14.en: Origen * "When he shall fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing" [21]. The mouth of the righteous will be filled with laughter when the tears of their journey are completed, and their hearts will be filled completely with the shout of eternal joy. Concerning this laughter the Truth says to His disciples: "Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy" (Jn 16:20). Again: "But I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you" (Jn 16:22). Concerning this laughter of the holy Church Solomon says: [She laughs in the last day] (Prov 31:25). It was also said that it will go well in the end with him who fears the Lord. There is no bodily laughter there, but the laughter of the heart...

8.18.0.en: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought [22].

8.18.1.en: * [Thy adversaries shall be clothed with shame], whether visible or invisible... The Egyptian was clothed with shame when he saw Joseph (Gen 39:20-21). Jezebel was in the same state when she saw Elijah sharing in the position of the saints, him whom she had persecuted with tyranny (1 Kgs 19:2); likewise the adversaries of Job who were not victorious were also clothed with shame when they saw Job rejoicing among the angels.

8.18.2.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * As they see before the eyes of their mind their past evil deeds flowing forth, iniquity clothes them on every side, and drags them down by its weight. Then they suffer from the memory of their evils while they are being punished.

8.18.4.en: Let me possess You, O Wisdom of God!

8.18.5.en: * Your love brought You down to us, O Wisdom of God, for You are my light and my treasure and the secret of my joy and my peace.

8.18.6.en: You drew near to me, and longed to dwell within me.

8.18.7.en: Enter and dwell in me, that I may possess You forever.

8.18.8.en: * Without You, who will restrain my tongue so that it is not babbling?

8.18.9.en: I can tame wild beasts, but who will tame my tongue but You?

8.18.10.en: You fill my depths with Your riches, so that I feel no emptiness.

8.18.11.en: I am filled with You, so I do not hunger for vain talk.

8.18.12.en: You fill me with the pledge of Your glory, so I judge no one!

8.18.13.en: I possess You, and so I possess divine love.

8.18.14.en: I keep silent, that I may speak with You about every human being.

8.18.15.en: I love, and so I desire the glory of every person.

8.18.16.en: * Let me possess You, for You are the Crucified; let me walk as a member of Your Church, the suffering Bride.

8.18.17.en: I find my delight and my riches and my joy in being crucified with You.

8.18.18.en: False philosophical enticements will not draw me away, nor will the enemy of good ensnare me by denying the Church, Your Bride.

8.18.19.en: Nor do I seek temporal rest and passing happiness at the expense of eternal glory.

8.18.20.en: You keep Your suffering Church bearing the spirit of victory.

8.18.21.en: You are in her midst, so she shall never be moved!

8.18.22.en: * Let me possess You, that I may present You to every wounded sinner.

8.18.23.en: I present You in the language of love and gentleness, in Your wisdom, not in the language of biting criticism and wounding.

8.18.24.en: You covered me; grant me to cover my brethren.

8.18.25.en: You lifted me from hell to Paradise; grant me to embrace in love those who fell with me.

8.18.26.en: Wonderful is Your salvation, and wonderful is Your wisdom!

8.18.27.en: Make me, through You, wise and wonderful in my love for my brethren!

8.18.28.en: * Teach me, O divine Wisdom, how to pray to You.

8.18.29.en: Inflame my heart with Your love, so that I will ask for nothing but to possess You, and that all humanity may possess You with me.

8.18.30.en: What do You offer me but Your dwelling in me.

8.18.31.en: What do I hope for but to be united with You.

8.18.32.en: What reward is there for me, except the enjoyment of You!

8.18.33.en: Grant me Your wisdom, that I may possess You, and through You possess everything, by Your indwelling within me!

8.18.34.en: * When will You come, O divine Wisdom, that I may enjoy a glorious end, and enjoy the fellowship of the heavenly glories.

8.18.35.en: You will carry me to the bosom of the Father, and my soul will rest there eternally.

8.18.36.en: My labors will turn into heavenly rest, and my sufferings into perpetual sweetness, and my daily deaths into the joy of the resurrection!

8.18.37.en: * Grant me, O Lord, that You shine upon me with Your light, that I may know Your surpassing mysteries.

8.18.38.en: Let me experience them richly by Your grace, let me taste them in my life as through the experience of my fathers.

8.18.39.en: Let Your wisdom work in me as in my fathers.

8.18.40.en: Not that I should hold to the words of my fathers without their life.

8.18.41.en: Grant me a holy heart that receives the holy deposit, and hands it on, not in literalisms and formalities, but in the spirit of truth and holiness.

8.18.42.en: * Let me drink of the waters of Your Holy Spirit, that I may be like an olive tree planted in Your house.

8.18.43.en: The enemy will not be able to approach it, nor will his trials make it lose its vitality and growth.

8.18.44.en: I drink in Your constant remembrance, and Your name will not depart from my lips.

8.18.45.en: And may Your image not be removed from my heart!

8.18.46.en: I remember You always and am filled with hope.

8.18.47.en: I hide in You, and find safety and peace.

8.18.48.en: Instead of the spider's house that I wove for myself, let me dwell in Your embrace, O fortress of my life.

8.18.49.en: * By You, O Wisdom of God, all hypocrisy departs from me.

8.18.50.en: So I will not be like the papyrus that grows in waters containing mud, but like a tree planted by the streams of Your Holy Spirit.

8.18.51.en: Nor will I be like the spider protected by a flimsy house, but I will dwell in You, O source of all safety.

8.18.52.en: I will not be like grass that the sun burns and dries, but I will enjoy Your light shining on my depths.

8.18.53.en: Nor will I stumble over stones in the road, but I will become a living stone in the heavenly Temple.

8.18.54.en: Nor will I be like a leafy tree whose roots the axe has struck, but an olive tree planted in Your holy house.

8.18.55.en: * In You my soul rejoices, in You I enjoy the pledge of the joy of heaven!

8.18.56.en: In You I become the wise, holy bride.

9.0.s.en: 1. No one will be justified before God

9.0.1.en: I know it is so of a truth.

9.1.0.en: But how should man be just with God? [2]

9.1.1.en: Job did not defend himself against Bildad's accusation of speaking too much (Job 8:2). He also revealed to him that he agrees with him in the principle: [God does not pervert judgment, and the pious are kept by the care of God, and the wicked man perishes by his wickedness](a).

9.1.2.en: But he asked: "How should man be just with God?" This question does not carry a spirit of murmuring, nor does it carry a revolt against the severity of God, but he confessed the reality that if God dealt with us according to our deserts, all mankind would perish, for there is none righteous in the eyes of God, no, not one.

9.1.3.en: If Job looks at himself, comparing himself with those around him, he sees that he is righteous, but when he looks at God the Holy and Righteous, he finds himself not pure, and unable to be justified before Him. For even His holy angels will not be justified before Him. The Psalmist says: "And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified" (Ps 2:143).

9.1.4.en: No one will be able to be justified before God except His eternal Word, who became man without sin alone; he who hides in Him bears His righteousness, and so is justified before the Lord.

9.1.5.en: The Apostle says: "But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption" (1 Cor 30:1), "And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness" (Eph 24:4).

9.1.6.en: * Look how Job also confesses his sins (Job 9:2-3, 19-20, 30; 13:26 - 14:5; 16:14, 17). He says that he is certain that there is no righteous man before the Lord. So he is certain of this also, that if we say that we have no sin, the truth is not in us. While God gives a lofty testimony about his righteousness in terms of the level of human conduct, Job himself knows the truth that it is so, where he says: "How should a mortal be just before the Lord? If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him."

9.1.7.en: St. Augustine * We see him, through his words, expressing himself in a wonderful manner as pious and virtuous, presenting his conduct as his offering to God, adapting his words for the sake of the glory of God. Even when he speaks from himself, or when his wife provoked him, and when his friends angered him, and even when the accuser (the devil) pulled at his throat to make him blaspheme, the righteous man did not cease to glorify God. "I will bless the Lord at all times" (Ps 34:1).

9.1.8.en: In a better way Job corrected the words of his companions who insulted him, turning everything they uttered against the wrestler in spite and contempt toward the excellent Job into a blessing for God's sake. If you say: How so? Learn this, for Bildad, with a spiteful intention in his statement, began with this introduction: [Doth the Lord pervert judgment, or doth the Maker of all things reverse the right?] (Job 8:3) What could Job say to this? How does he answer his adversary, turning in a wonderful way what was meant to throw him down? Let us listen: "Then Job answered and said: [True, I know that it is so. But how should mortal man be just with the Lord?] [1-2].

9.1.9.en: Why do you insult Job as one who is not righteous?

9.1.10.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * Job answered them: "True, I know that it is so. But how should mortal man be just with God? For if he will contend with him, he will not hear him, nor will he answer him one word in a thousand, for he is wise in understanding and strong and great; who is hard enough to be able to stand before him? Who makes the mountains grow old, and they know not! And who overturns them in his anger. Who shakes the earth from its foundations, and its pillars tremble! He speaks to the sun, and it rises not, and sets his seal upon the stars. Who alone stretches out the heavens and walks upon the sea as on level ground, maker of the Bier (or Pleiades) and the Evening star and the Mighty (Great) Bear, Great Bear, and the chambers of the horses.

9.1.11.en: [Doer of great things past finding out, and wonders without number, glorious and without measure or number. If he passes over me I do not see him, and if he goes by me I do not perceive how?] (Job 2:9-11) LXX. How much stronger was his trumpet when he made him cry out concerning the power of the Lord! But in this strength the righteous man receives help, not destruction. Truly, while it seems that it is the power of the Lord that is described, in reality the mysteries of our redemption are being revealed!

9.1.12.en: St. Ambrose * It is the treasure that was given to them in this life to possess within their souls, who [of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption] (1 Cor 1:30). He who has found the treasure of the heavenly Spirit and possesses it fulfills by it all the righteousness of the commandment and all the fulfilling of virtues in purity and without blame, indeed easily and without compulsion.

9.1.13.en: Therefore let us entreat God, and ask and request of Him with a sense of need, that He may bestow on us the treasure of His Spirit, so that we may walk in all His commandments in purity and without blame, and fulfil all the righteousness of the Spirit in purity and perfection, by means of the heavenly treasure, who is Christ.

9.1.14.en: St. Macarius the Great * When a man submits to God he receives righteousness, but he who stands against Him loses righteousness. For he who compares himself with the source of all good things deprives himself of the goodness he has received. He who ascribes to himself the blessings given him by God wages war against God with the very gifts of God.

9.1.16.en: * The righteousness of God is Christ; the Apostle says: [who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption]; as it is written, [He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord].

9.1.17.en: The righteousness of God, which is the gift of grace without merits, is not known by those who want to establish their own righteousness, and so do not submit themselves to the righteousness of God, which is Christ.

9.1.18.en: In this righteousness we find the wealth of God's sweetness, of which the Psalm says: [Taste and see how sweet the Lord is] (Ps 34:8).

9.2.0.en: 3 If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand. 4 He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and remained safe? 5 Which removeth the mountains, and they know not, which overturneth them in his anger. 6 Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble. 7 Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars. 8 Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea. 9 Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south. 10 Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number. 11 "Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not. 12 Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou? 13 God will not withdraw his anger; the helpers of Rahab stoop under him."

9.2.1.en: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand [3].

9.2.2.en: No man can compete with his Creator in discussion or in struggle. A man cannot answer one question out of the thousand questions that God puts to him. God spoke with Job and put several questions to him, and Job stood unable to answer any one of them (Job 38-39). Thus the wisdom of man stands silent in helplessness before the surpassing wisdom of God.

9.2.3.en: God directs a thousand accusations to man, and man finds no answer to justify what he does in even one matter of the thousand, for God does not err in His judgment. And He knows our depths more than we know ourselves. We have nothing to do but lay our hands on our mouths as Job did (Job 40:4-5).

9.2.4.en: * Did I not confess my transgressions to You, my God, and You took away the iniquity of my heart? I do not contend in judgment with You, for You are the Truth. I do not wish to deceive myself, lest my iniquity lie against itself. Therefore I do not dispute Your judgments, because "If thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities... who shall stand?" (Ps 130:3).

9.2.5.en: * I do not dispute in judgment with You, who are the Truth. I will not deceive myself, lest my iniquities stand against the Truth. Therefore I will not contend in judgment with You. For if You mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand before You? (Ps 3:130).

9.2.6.en: * God alone is righteous and the One who justifies; He gives man righteousness.

9.2.7.en: They seek to establish their own righteousness, meaning that they think that goodness is from themselves and not a divine gift. In this they have not "submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God" (Rom 10:3), because they are proud and think they are able to please God by themselves and not by what is God's.

9.2.8.en: St. Augustine * In Holy Scripture the number 1000 usually refers to "the sum total".... The Psalmist says: [the word which he commanded to a thousand generations] (Ps 105:8)... So it was said of John the Seer: [shall reign with him a thousand years] (Rev 20:6), because the reign of the holy Church is accomplished where it becomes perfect in its totality...

9.2.9.en: Now he who contends with God does not belong to Him, but ascribes to himself the glory of his goodness. May the holy man consider that whatever he has actually received, even the gifts greatest in importance, if he is glorified, it is only because of what he received as a gift... And let him say: "If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand." For he who contends with his Creator is unable to answer Him one in a thousand. For the man who places himself in the position of perfection proves that he lacks even the very beginning of the good life.

9.2.11.en: * [If thou, Lord, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand?] (Ps 3:130). That is, everyone says: "I am a sinner, I am full of countless sins, I cannot approach God and pray and call upon Him"... It is impossible for anyone to give a precise account of his affairs, but he seeks mercy and compassion. We say this, not to draw souls into indifference, but to offer consolation to those who have fallen into despair. [Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?] (Prov 9:20) Let him remember: [Who trusts that he is free from sins?].

9.2.12.en: St. John Chrysostom He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength.

9.3.0.en: Who hath hardened himself against him, and remained safe? [4]

9.3.1.en: If anyone dares and persists in his stubbornness and rebellion against God, he certainly reaps the fruit of his folly. All who defied and did not repent were not safe, nor did they find peace in their depths, rest in their way, or success in their works. All resistance to God is like grass or thorns that defy the fire and are burned and perish (Isa 27:4; Ezek 28:24).

9.3.2.en: The angels who hardened themselves against God were not safe (2 Pet 2:4). And since the dragon fought against God, he was cast down to the earth (Rev 12:7-9). So rebellious sinners [treasure up unto themselves wrath against the day of wrath] (Rom 2:5).

9.3.3.en: It is utter madness for a man to stand up to resist God or to contend against the All-wise and All-powerful, who knows everything and is able to do everything.

9.3.4.en: He who wants true peace does not enter into strife with God, but receives the Lord Christ, who is our peace, who gives us reconciliation with God His Father, and with our souls and with our brethren, and even with nature itself.

9.3.5.en: * [For he is wise in heart, and mighty in strength.] What wonder if we call the Creator of the wise wise, He whom we know to be Wisdom itself? And what astonishment that he describes Him as "mighty", since He is Power itself? But the saint, in praising the Creator with these two words, conveys meaning to us as he calls us to tremble at our knowledge of ourselves. For God is called "wise" since He knows perfectly the secrets of our hearts, and he adds "mighty", since He is known to strike them with power. Therefore He is not deceived by us since He is wise, and we cannot flee from Him because He is strong...

9.3.6.en: [Who resists him and has peace?] For the Creator of all things wonderfully governs them Himself, so that having been created they work together in harmony. Therefore any resistance against God breaks the harmony together in peace, and these things cannot be governed well, since they lose the government from above. If these things submit to God they continue in peace, and if left to themselves they work in confusion... The first father of the human race, when he disobeyed the commandment of his Creator, was exposed to the arrogance of the flesh, and when he did not submit to his Creator in obedience to Him, he lowers himself until he loses the peace of the body...

9.3.7.en: Now it is said that we resist God when we oppose His providence. Not that our weakness resists His unchanging decrees, but what our weakness does has no strength to be accomplished. But if human weakness attempts it, it often knows the power of His providence, and yet aims at opposing it as far as it is able.

9.3.9.en: * He who seeks peace seeks Christ, for He is peace.

9.3.10.en: St. Basil the Great * He says: "(Christ) is our peace" (Eph 2:14). Elsewhere he calls Him a mediator. He of His own will mediates between two divided realms.

9.3.11.en: Souls born of the fountain of God's goodness were confined in the world. A barrier was found in the middle, a kind of fence. A barrier made by the deceptions of the flesh and worldly lusts. And Christ, by His mystery, by His Cross and passion and way of life, broke down this barrier. He conquered sin and taught that it must be broken down.

9.3.12.en: He took away the barrier from the midst. He overcame the enmity in His flesh. The work is not ours. We were not called to free ourselves.

9.3.13.en: Faith in Christ is our salvation.

9.4.0.en: Fr. Marius Victorinus Which removeth the mountains, and they know not, which overturneth them in his anger [5].

9.4.1.en: We often look at the mountains in nature and think them firm and settled, that no one can move or shift them, so they were called "the everlasting mountains" (Hab 3:6), and the sun and the world seem fixed by their laws, but when the Lord wills, heaven and earth pass away, and the mountains too are moved by a word from Him. Our God is "He who removeth the mountains, and they know not", that is, whether they wish it or not. He is the God of the impossible; before Him Mount Sinai trembled (Ps 68:8), the mountains skipped (Ps 114:4), and the everlasting mountains were broken or scattered (Hab 3:6).

9.4.2.en: "The mountains shall be moved from their foundations with the waters, the rocks shall melt as wax at thy presence" (Jdt 16:18).

9.4.3.en: "The earth shook and trembled; the foundations of the mountains trembled and were shaken, because he was wroth" (Ps 18:7).

9.4.4.en: "The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of the whole earth" (Ps 5:97)

9.4.5.en: "He toucheth the mountains, and they smoke" (Ps 32:104).

9.4.6.en: "The mountains skipped like rams, and the little hills like lambs" (Ps 4:114).

9.4.7.en: "Come down, touch the mountains, and they shall smoke" (Ps 5:144).

9.4.8.en: * What are the mountains that the Lord made grow old? They are Moses and Aaron and Joshua the son of Nun and Gideon and the prophets and all the men of the books of the Old Testament. The Lord Jesus came, and brought the New Testament, and what He had made (before) became old. The Christian was renewed and the Jew grew old; grace was renewed, and the letter grew old. The mountains were moved and removed. Yes, He moved the understanding according to the letter, and overthrew it, and established the perception according to the Spirit. Therefore the understanding of the Law according to the flesh has passed away and the Law became spiritual. Therefore the Apostle says: "For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal" (Rom 7:14). But he himself who was carnal became spiritual, as the Apostle affirms, saying: "and I think also that I have the Spirit of God" (1 Cor 7:40). Thus Jesus made these mountains grow old and the Jews did not know it. Indeed had they known it they would not have crucified the Lord of glory, nor followed Jewish fables.

9.4.9.en: St. Ambrose * We say that the Jews, although they previously enjoyed God's favor, being loved by Him more than others, yet this divine dispensation and grace have passed to us, when Jesus transferred the authority working among the Jews to the believers from the Gentiles.

9.4.10.en: * When Jesus addressed the Jews, saying: "The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof" (Mt 21:43), what other dispensation was He, by His divine authority, about to present, except that He pushed the whole Jewish Scripture - which contained the mysteries of the Kingdom of God - into the circle of light.

9.4.11.en: * We who were transferred from the Law and the Prophets to the Gospel have been circumcised again (Josh 7:5) (by the rock) which is Christ (1 Cor 4:10), so the word of the Lord to Joshua was fulfilled in us, "This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you" (Josh 9:5).

9.4.12.en: Origen * He says: The mountains do not know it. And as David said: "He toucheth the mountains, and they smoke" (Ps 104:32). In this phrase he speaks of the power of God, saying that He is able to do all things in the strength of His wrath. For Job gives testimony to His justice, as he also gives testimony to His power.

9.4.13.en: St. John Chrysostom * [He uses the mountains, and they know not, He who overturns them in His wrath.] [He uses] the visible mountains in truth when He wants to change the face of visible creation. But it is no wonder for these (mountains) that they do not know that they are "used", for they were not given a mind like human beings and living angels. Therefore Job calls the power of the arrogant demons mountains. Therefore the prophet Jeremiah calls the accuser (the devil) [a destroying mountain, which destroyeth all the earth] (Jer 51:25). For the corruption of the demons is base. Although they are full of deceit, they cannot reach the thoughts of God, since He wants to hide His thoughts from them, nor did they perceive the fall that befell them. What Paul says is an example of this: "Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought: But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory: Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" (1 Cor 2:6-8).

9.5.0.en: He who uses these (powers) in the conflicts of the mystery of the Cross is the One who created them (Col 1:16), and destroyed them (Amos 3:14), and not only destroyed them but "in His anger" demolished their altars, scattered their temples, and ruined their statues. In victory, He stripped them of their glory (Col 2:15), for not only did the demons usurp glory (Rev 13:4-8), when they ought not to have done this, but they also corrupted humanity along with them. But when does true, just destruction befall them, as in complete wrath? When this visible world ends. In any case, if you say, how does He do this? You will learn it from the following: "Which shaketh the earth out of her place" [6].

9.5.1.en: Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem God in His love for mankind raises up from His true believers holy, firm mountains, which are like Mount Sinai where the Lord appeared and gave His law to Moses, or like Mount Tabor where He was transfigured in the midst of His Church, which includes the men of the Old Testament, represented by Moses and Elijah, and the men of the New Testament, represented by Peter, James and John. On the other hand, the wicked who resist the Lord, who do not submit to Him, even if they think themselves to be firm mountains, their foundations tremble before the Lord in His wrath, and by His fury He makes them shake; He touches them with His wrath and they smoke. They skip like rams from before His face, and melt like wax before the fire.

9.5.2.en: * "The earth shook and trembled" (Ps 7:18). When the Son of Man was glorified thus, sinners shook and trembled. "The foundations of the mountains trembled" (Ps 7:18), for the hope of the proud who were in this life trembled. "And were shaken because he was wroth." This is the hope in temporal blessings, which is no longer founded in the hearts of men.

9.5.3.en: * "The hills melted like wax before the Lord" (Ps 5:97). Who are the hills? The proud. Everything that exalts itself against God, through Christ and the Christians, trembles and submits... Where is the haughtiness of the powers? Where is the cruelty of the unbelievers? The Lord was to them a fire, and they melted at His presence like wax. They were hard until the fire worked.

9.5.4.en: St. Augustine * "The mountains melted like wax" (Ps 5:97). To me the mountains seem to be the powers of the demons. Whether they are mountains or not, they are certainly the proud people.

9.5.5.en: This fire does not destroy those below (the humble) but destroys only the haughty. As a matter of fact, lightning rarely affects those in the valley, but those on high on the mountains will not escape it.

9.5.6.en: St. Jerome St. Ambrose presents to us a wonderful concept of the moving of the mountains while they know not, for when He came into the world He moved the holy mountains, as He moved our concepts of Moses the prophet who received the Law and of the prophets and the men of the Old Testament. He moved them from the literal Jewish mind that we might receive them in the Spirit through the Gospel. For although the Jews hold to the Law and the Fathers and the Prophets, they do not know the mystery of God and His hidden wisdom, because they still see them through the veil placed on the face of Moses(b). All this was moved to become our portion, so that we may understand and know the mystery of God's eternal plan and His surpassing wisdom and His dispensation for our salvation. This is what the Apostle Paul cherished after he met the Lord Christ and the mountains were moved for him, and he gained insight into the divine mystery, so that he could not keep silent.

9.5.7.en: "Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ" (Eph 4:3).

9.5.8.en: "That the Lord would open unto us a door... to speak the mystery of Christ" (Col 3:4).

9.5.9.en: "That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love, and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ" (Col 2:2).

9.5.10.en: "And to make all men see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the ages hath been hid in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ" (Eph 9:3).

9.5.11.en: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble [6].

9.5.12.en: If the earth seems to be settled on pillars that no one can shake, yet at the command of its Creator it is shaken, and there is nothing to support it.

9.5.13.en: In the symbolic sense, we saw that the mountains are moved in the sense that the haughty who dwell on the mountaintops are exposed to destruction through the divine lightnings. On the other hand, the Law and the Fathers and the Prophets are high holy mountains, that move from the hands of the Jews, literal in their understanding, to the sons of the New Testament, to whom the divine wisdom has been revealed, and who have come to know the hidden mystery of Christ. By the same logic, the earth points to the wicked who have become dust like their father the first Adam, to whom it was said: [Dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return](c). Now that the Heavenly One has come down to our earth, and dwelt among us, and become as one of us, we enjoy the heavenly life, and we hear the divine voice: [Heaven thou art, and unto heaven shalt thou return].

9.5.14.en: And dwelt among us, and became as one of us, we enjoy the heavenly life, and we hear the divine voice: [Heaven thou art, and unto heaven shalt thou return].

9.5.15.en: * The stranger centurion knows, while the Levite who was of His own did not know. The Gentile worshiped Him, and the Hebrew denied Him. Therefore it is not unreasonable that the pillars of the world moved (Job 9:6) when the chief priests did not believe.

9.5.16.en: The pillars moved in order that new pillars might take their place. As though God Himself deemed it fitting to say: [I have set up the pillars of it] (Ps 75:3). Learn what pillars He set up: "James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship" (Gal 2:9).

9.5.17.en: St. Ambrose * With vessels and a bucket one measures the water that comes out of natural springs, but the water that flows from spiritual springs is measured by our understanding and our burning desire and our reverence, by which we draw near to them. He who walks in this order at once carries countless blessings, for the grace of God works in him invisibly, and lightens the burden of his conscience, and brings him to abundant safety, and then prepares him to withdraw from the shore of the earth and bear the anchor of heaven. For a man who still embraces his body can have nothing attached to the earth, but sets before his eyes all the delights of heaven and contemplates them without ceasing.

9.5.18.en: * I want you to keep your minds on these things always (Col 1:3). For our concern with them frees us from the earth and transports us to heaven.

9.5.19.en: St. John Chrysostom * It is right for us to be there in the presence of God in the heavens, we who learned the lesson while on earth, and went there to heaven in order to be in the love of God the Father, whom we came to know while on earth, and because God the Word, the Holy One, made everything and taught us and teaches us everything, and trains us in all good things.

9.5.20.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * Abraham left his city and his relatives by a divine command, but his migration suited him as a prophet, its aim being the seeking of the knowledge of God.

9.5.21.en: In truth it was not a bodily migration - as I think - but was preparing him for the knowledge of those things which the Spirit discovers.

9.5.22.en: By leaving his homeland, that is, by going out of himself, out of the circle of base and earthly thoughts, Abraham raised his mind as far as possible above the common limits of human nature, and let go of the soul's attachment to the senses.

9.5.23.en: Thus, since the attachments of the senses did not hinder him, his mind became pure, perceiving what is unseen, and hearing and sight no longer caused his mind to err because of appearances.

9.5.24.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * When the will of God is accomplished by us who are on earth as it is accomplished by those in heaven, we become like the heavenly ones, as we bear like them the image of the heavenly (1 Cor 49:15) and inherit the Kingdom of Heaven (Mt 34:25). And those after us who are on earth come, praying that they may be like us when we are in heaven (Paradise).

9.5.25.en: Origen * You must long for heaven, and the things that are in heaven, indeed even before heaven, for we have been commanded to make the earth heaven, and to behave and speak in all things as though we were speaking there, while we are on earth. This also must be the aim of our prayer which we offer to the Lord. Nothing hinders our reaching the perfection of the heavenly powers because we dwell on earth; rather it is possible, even while we dwell here, to do everything as though we were already dwelling on high.

9.5.26.en: * Truly the Lord came to abolish the old things and to call us to a greater homeland.

9.5.27.en: He does everything to set us free from unnecessary things and from our affection for the earth. For this reason He also referred to the pagans, saying: "For after all these things do the Gentiles seek" (Mt 6:32); who devote all their labor to the present life, and have no care for the things to come, nor for any heavenly thought.

9.6.0.en: St. John Chrysostom Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars [7].
